episode_title: Is Your Business Really Worth What You Think? | Gregory Kovsky

real_qa.q: What percentage of a business owner's time and labor is typically unaccounted for when calculating company value?
real_qa.r: Many business owners fail to recognize how many hours and full-time equivalents they personally contribute to the business. Gregory gave the example of a highly productive florist in Louisiana who was so efficient she could complete 10 designs while average florists completed 4-5, requiring 2 to 2.5 people to replace her when she sold. Owners often don't realize the void created when they leave, especially when seasoned entrepreneurs can make decisions in 20 minutes that would take a newcomer three hours.

real_qa.q: How many business transactions has International Business Associates completed since its founding?
real_qa.r: International Business Associates, the Pacific Northwest's oldest and largest business brokerage firm, has been involved in over 4,400 transactions across more than 50 years of operation.

real_qa.q: Why do serial entrepreneurs often sell their businesses before scaling to large team sizes?
real_qa.r: Gregory's client Mohamed in the tech space has sold four businesses because he loves small dedicated teams working hard on a product but dislikes when he needs an HR department and CFO. He typically reaches a certain scale, then sells so he can move on to new projects rather than manage large organizational structures. His preference is working with 3-8 people rather than 25.
real_qa.requete: serial entrepreneur exit before scaling team

real_qa.q: What is the main mistake business owners make when assessing their company's marketability?
real_qa.r: The biggest lie owners tell themselves is not recognizing how many hours and full-time equivalents they personally contribute to the business. They see strong financial returns but fail to disclose that a buyer would need to hire multiple people to replace their personal productivity, expertise, and decision-making speed. This creates a valuation gap between what the tax returns show and what a new owner can actually replicate.

real_qa.q: What credentials are required to operate a florist business in Louisiana?
real_qa.r: Louisiana is one of the only states in the nation where you need to be certified to be a florist and must pass a test to do so. This certification requirement shaped the business model of one of Gregory's clients, an exceptional Vietnamese florist whose personal expertise and efficiency made her business highly valuable but difficult to transition.
